title: Tighten concavity halo and emit rims as dedicated patches
description:
The concavity carve-out pass currently expands each concavity component by CONCAVITY_RING_EXPAND=1 face-ring so the rim renders as a distinct color change. On the skull this causes two issues:

1. Nasal cavity leakage: the 1-ring halo oversteps the cavity edge and absorbs part of the nasal floor / surrounding bone.
2. The halo dilutes the 'this is a concave region' signal — the expanded region mixes concave interior vertices with convex rim vertices, so the labeler sometimes sees a confused shape.

New behavior:
1. Drop CONCAVITY_RING_EXPAND to 0 (concavity patches are exactly the concave interior).
2. Emit a separate 'rim' patch along the high-curvature crease bounding each concavity. Rim patches are thin (1-2 face-rings wide) and get their own patch id.
3. Labeler prompt updated to explain this pairing: rim+bowl patches usually deserve a single anatomical label like 'right_eye_socket' (rim+bowl), so the prompt instructs Claude to recognize paired (concavity, rim) patches and label them accordingly — or give both the same semantic name with _rim / _bowl suffixes.

Originated from PATCH-1+2 follow-up user observation: 'the left nose cavity is still leaking'.
definition-of-done: Concavity patches are now strictly interior (no halo); paired rim patches surround each. Nose cavity stops leaking into adjacent bone. Eye sockets still come out clean.
testing-plan: uv run label-patches /tmp/skull.obj --force and verify: (a) nasal cavity vertices are strictly within the piriform aperture, no overflow; (b) rim patches appear as thin colored rings around the orbital plates and nasal cavity in the multiview.
